correctness.rationale: Read contact-center optimality proof: c must be convex combination of active points and equal-distance contacts; weighted sum of their squared distances is R²+||y−c||². For base-only contacts, α_i=(1−μ/b_i²)/2, μ=(p−2)/Σtail b_i^-2 and inactive b_j²≤μ force a tail. Apex inclusion compares κ_B against μ. In apex-active case inactive coordinates c_j=−at, active c_i=(b_i²−K)/(2b_i), and two linear equations uniquely give K_p,t_p; monotone b²+2atb forces the unique feasible tail, with slack inequalities certifying all vertices. Standard a=b_i=1 yields center −(d−1)/(2(d+1))1 and radius sqrt(d)(d+3)/(2(d+1)).
residual_risks: Higher-dimensional positive arbitrary real weights require the proof; exact finite enumeration covered only specific small rational tests.
